card.name: Second half of hyphenated compounds
card.fires_on: The piece right after a hyphen or inside a hyphenated compound, such as -one in one-on-one, -go in get-go, or tracted in placebo-subtracted. It also fires on the word after co- or post- type hyphens, like co-administration.

modes.label: Hyphenated compound ending
modes.description: The closing part of a hyphenated everyday phrase.
modes.example: live, one-on<<-one>> help when you need it with Straighter

modes.label: Hyphen-joined medical terms
modes.description: The part after a hyphen in clinical terms such as placebo-subtracted or co-administration.

modes.label: Hyphenated names
modes.description: The final part of a hyphenated name or word.
modes.example: allow Pac<<-Man>> to eat the ghosts.

card.writes: No clear output effect beyond a weak push toward varied word continuations.
card.plain: It lights up on the later part of a word that is joined by a hyphen, like one-on-one or co-administration.
